in_hebrew.name: סיבלה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: סיבלה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו בשבועת אלוהים, נגזר מהמילה העברית 'שבועה' ומהמילה היוונית 'σίβυλλα', המתייחסת לנביאה או לאדם בעל כוח נבואי. השם משמש כזכר ונקבה כאחד, ויש לו קונוטציות של התמסרות לאלוהים והשבעת שבועה לפניו.

in_greek.name: Σίβυλλα
in_greek.long_meaning: Η Σίβυλλα είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη για την 'προφήτισσα' ή 'Σίβυλλα', αναφερόμενο σε γυναίκα με δυνάμει προφητικές. Το όνομα συνδέεται με την παράδοση των πρώτων Χριστιανικών κοινοτήτων και την προφητική λειτουργία εντός της Εκκλησίας.

in_latin.name: Sibella
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Sibella originem ducit ex voce Latina 'iuramentum', quae est Deus. Nomen hoc in traditione Christiana adhibetur ad exprimendam devotionem et fidem in Deum. Est nomen quod et masculinum et femininum habetur.

in_english.name: Sibella
in_english.long_meaning: The name Sibella originates from the Hebrew word for 'oath' and the Greek term for 'prophetess'. Historically, the name has been used across various Christian cultures, symbolizing a bond of promise between the individual and God.

historical_references.reference: In Scottish mythology, Sibella was a fairy queen who resided in a crystal cavern near Loch Lomond. She was known for her great beauty and her ability to heal with the waters from her magic well. The legend of Sibella is closely associated with the Ballad of Sir Hugh, a chivalric tale of gallant knights and enchanted maidens.

Sibylla was a prophetess in the Roman religion, revered for her ability to foretell future events. She is said to have lived during the time of the Roman kings, and her prophecies were inscribed on tablets that were later discovered and deciphered by the poet Virgil. These prophecies played a significant role in the development of the Christian apocalyptic tradition.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Sibella, a variant of the biblical name sibyl, has seen a modern resurgence in popularity, driven by a renewed interest in historical names and a shift towards gender-neutral name usage. This name can be found on various baby names websites, as well as on social media platforms, where it is used as a unisex name. In literature, Sibella is a character in Margaret Atwood's novel 'Hag-Seed', adding to the name's contemporary relevance.
